title: Graphing a Reflected and Shifted Square Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = sqrt(9 - x) by identifying its parent function, transformation sequence, natural domain, range, and intercepts.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt{x} \text{ reflected across y-axis and shifted right } 9;\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 9],\quad \text{Range: } [0, \infty),\quad \text{Endpoint: } (9, 0),\quad \text{y-intercept: } (0, 3)

steps.title: Factor the Radicand to Reveal the Transformation Sequence
steps.explanation: Factoring out -1 inside the radical expresses y = sqrt(9 - x) as taking y = sqrt(x), reflecting across the y-axis to get y = sqrt(-x), and then shifting 9 units to the right by replacing x with x - 9.
steps.why: Writing f(9 - x) = f(-(x - 9)) separates the y-axis reflection from the horizontal translation.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: Requiring the radicand 9 - x >= 0 yields x <= 9, so the domain is (-infinity, 9]. The principal square root takes all non-negative real values [0, infinity).
steps.why: Even roots require non-negative radicands, and 9 - x covers [0, infinity) as x varies over (-infinity, 9].

steps.title: Find the Endpoint and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The graph has its right endpoint at (9, 0) and rises to the left through (5, 2) and the y-intercept (0, 3).
steps.why: Setting x = 9 gives y = 0, and setting x = 0 gives y = 3.
